text:
maria: heads up - after the GPU pool scaled down in eu-edge, we started seeing intermittent 503s from the inference headless svc (namespace=serving). traces show requests hitting kube-proxy but no backend pod selected :/
aj: what do `kubectl get endpointslice -n serving -l kubernetes.io/service-name=inference` and `kubectl get endpoints -n serving` show?

maria: endpoints list empty for that headless service but pods are Running and have IPs (checked on nodes). endpointslice still shows old entries pointing to drained nodes 

sre-leo: sounds like EndpointSlice controller didn't update after node drain. saw kube-proxy CPU spike + iptables churn on the drained nodes earlier. could be conntrack/backpressure during large drain burst :grimacing: 

dena: echoing - we saw similar when spot evictions happened fast. kube-proxy kept old endpoint routes until ipvs/iptables housekeeping cleared which left a window of 503s. quick checks: `kubectl exec -n kube-system -it <kube-proxy-pod> -- conntrack -L | grep <pod-ip>` and `ss -ntap` on the node to confirm stale NAT sessions

infra-bot: autoscaler: scaledown event for eu-edge-gpu-pool at 2024-09-18T02:11Z - removed 4 nodes 

aj: can you paste `kubectl describe endpointslice -n serving <slice-name>` for one of the stale slices? also include `kubectl get pods -o wide -n serving --selector=app=inference` output

maria: pasted outputs in thread (snip) -- slices still list the drained node IPs under endpointAddresses, but those nodes are gone. controller manager logs show warnings about "failed to update endpointslice" timeouts around the scale event

sre-leo: two quick mitigation ideas: 1) rotate kube-proxy daemonset on eu-edge (rollout restart) to force rules reconciliation 2) trigger the endpointslice controller to re-sync (restart controller manager pod handling endpoint slices)

dena: +1 for kube-proxy restart first (less impact). command we used before: `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/kube-proxy -n kube-system --selector=topology.kubernetes.io/region=eu-edge` (will pick only eu-edge nodes)

aj: also recommend bumping scale-down grace / parallelism on the autoscaler to avoid big bursts. set `--max-empty-bulk-delete` / equivalent limit or add a drain-delay annotation for inference node pool to let EndpointSlice controller catch up

maria: doing kube-proxy restart now on a single AZ, will monitor. if that doesn't reconcile, we'll restart the endpointslice controller.

sre-leo: post-restart steps: watch `kubectl get endpointslice -n serving -w` and `kubectl get endpoints -n serving -w` and tail kube-proxy logs for reconciliation messages. also watch per-node conntrack table size via metrics to ensure no saturation

dena: noted. follow-up: we should add a test to the chaos harness that simulates rapid node removal and asserts EndpointSlice->Endpoints convergence within Xs so this doesn't recur silently

maria: update: after restarting kube-proxy on one node, endpointslice for that region reconciled within ~20s and traffic is healthy again. rolling through the rest. leaving this thread for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
